title.narrative: Output 3.4. Increased capacity of ILO constituents to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

description.narrative:
Between January and August 2021, a total of 16,600 work days were generated through employment-intensive investment programmes (EIIP) in the following sectors: cultural heritage, solid waste sorting and irrigation channels maintenance.
Moreover, 41 persons were training within this period on EIIP approaches, of which 8 women.
The Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MOLSA) provided employment services for 4,534 job seekers, ultimately placing 703 internally displaced persons (IDP), refugee and host community members in jobs.
In-camp refugee's access to the labour market is facilitated through employment services, including 72 job placements (59 women) in agriculture, waste management and remedial services. The ILO provided technical support to the Directorate of Irrigation and Municipalities to implement EIIP interventions through the PROSPECTS project in Iraq, funded by the Netherlands.
Also, the ILO provided technical support for the UNESCO partners at the Cultural Heritage project in Erbil to integrate EIIP approaches at the project's activities.
Technical support was provided for the design, contracting and implementation/ monitoring of the activities, as well as providing technical trainings and seminars for the national stakeholders.
The ILO signed a memorandum of understanding with MOLSA, which included enhancing employment services in Dohuk. The ILO supported the hiring of employment and outreach officers, and trained them on effective employment service delivery. These officers served as Employment Officers and sit next to MOLSA Employment Officers to implement capacity building, outreach to employers and engagement with refugee and IDP job seekers.
Through an implementation agreement with an Iraq-based NGO, SWEDO, the ILO set up an employment unit inside the Domiz refugee camp, using UNHCR's community centre. Support staff were trained on employment services, and routine follow-up was done through the ILO PROSPECTS project office in Erbil.

description.narrative:
Rapid Assessment of the Impact of COVID-19 on Vulnerable Populations and Small-Scale Enterprises in Iraq was completed, validated by the government (Ministry of labour and social affairs) and published in July 2020. The target groups of the rapid assessment are households and enterprises that received support as part of programmes and projects implemented by humanitarian and development organisations in the Kurdistan region of Iraq (KRI) and the North regions.
Policy recommendation and recovery measures were addressed and shared in a national conference held in July 2021. Inputs and contributions from constituents and academics enriched the content of the final draft of the assessment. A draft social security law is being discussed at the parliament and ILO is actively engaged in the discussion to extend the coverage of social security to workers in the informal economy, with the rapid assessment providing inputs for this discussion. (https://www.ilo.org/beirut/media-centre/news/WCMS_806550/lang--en/index.htm). Indeed, the assessment aimed mainly to evaluate the immediate impact of COVID-19 on the labour market, while it attempted to recommend some broader measures for capturing longer term impacts such as the design and piloting of strategies for the extension of social insurance to vulnerable workers in the informal economy based on a series of feasibility assessments leading to targeted pilot testing of alternative modalities/ approaches for extension of coverage for different categories of workers (e.g. irregular workers, seasonal workers, self-employed, migrant workers), and specific sectors (potentially in the construction and agriculture sectors). A need to plan follow up surveys to cover the medium- and long-term impacts of socio-economic crises affect the Iraqi economy has been identified. The ILO completed a phase one "informality diagnostic" through an implementing partner FAFO. ILO ensured the progress follow up through period meetings, provided guidance related to the quantitative research techniques, assessment tools, training of interviewers and the data collection process and any other technical issues. The ILO performed proofreading of the report before dissemination to ensure the satisfaction with ILO's standards and ethical standards and had major role in designing the policy recommendation briefs. Importantly, the ILO supported the validation of assessment's findings with the Iraqi government represented by ministry of labour and social affairs and with international partners from the Cash Consortium for Iraq (DRC, NRC, IRC, Oxfam and Mercy Corps) by chairing online meetings for sharing the main findings, and by coordinating the collection of their technical inputs to the report.
